claim: Paired by trial index, go2-c2's plane gate reads 18/20 [0.683, 0.9877] where the count-dependent draw read 20/20 [0.8316, 1.0]: it still passes the gate's own tolerance rule (0.90 against the certificate's 0.95 minus 0.10), but the strict cliff rule can no longer attribute it, because at 20 trials only 20/20 clears the certificate's exact lower bound of 0.8308. The earlier ranking (latency 2 ticks, then kd x4) stands as a reading of the old draw only.
instrument: plain MuJoCo 3.11.0 + onnxruntime driven by the manifest alone, CPU, the WSL machine (Ubuntu under WSL2, x86_64); 20 held twists at seed 1000, each trial drawn from its own (seed, trial) stream (deploy.gate.DRAW_NOW = per-trial/2)

outcome.attribution_paired_draw: refused: the untouched baseline reads 18/20 [0.683, 0.9877], under the certificate's lower bound 0.8308
outcome.attribution_count_draw: most sensitive to latency 2 ticks, then kd 4 x (gate-attribution-go2-c2-2026-09-24)
outcome.preflight_paired_draw: passed 7/7 in simulation; peak torque demand 0.56x the force range (RL_calf) over the gate's first four paired twists, 0.45x under the old draw's
outcome.first_draw_bug: the first per-trial draw made a generator per axis, so a trial's three axes moved together; it read 16/20 and failed before the fix (one generator per trial, pinned in tests/test_review_deploy.py)

inputs.deployment: go2-c2-deploy-cited (policy go2-c2-model_1499@99b1655e2cec, robot go2@5003bf617b5f); its stamp now leaves run records out: go2-c2-deploy-cited@9eb3f5d5844c

artifacts.gate: docs/artifacts/go2/deploy/go2-c2-deploy-cited/gate.json; recorded at projects/go2-walk/deploy/go2-c2-deploy-cited/gate.json (the WSL machine; projects/ is not tracked)
artifacts.old_records: the 2026-09-12 gate record was replaced by the re-run (its numbers are kept here, gate_count_draw); attribution.json beside the manifest is still the count-draw record, and the card marks it 'drawn by count (re-run to pair)'

caveats: Sim only; nothing here is a hardware claim.

Both failed trials are near-zero forward commands (0.04 and 0.08 m/s) whose tracking error is judged as a ratio of the command, the shape where the ratio rule is harshest; the gate's rule is unchanged.
20 trials: 18/20 and 20/20 are one draw each; the two gates' intervals overlap.
The cliff rule is the operator's open choice: the gate's own tolerance rule would let the sweep run; this record changes neither rule.
The DDS gate record (gate-dds.json, 2026-09-13) is still the count-dependent draw and the card says so; re-running it needs /dev/uinput writable (docs/77 §7).
